newsitem.title: GERMANY: Main German parties score gains in Hesse poll.
newsitem.headline: Main German parties score gains in Hesse poll.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats and the opposition Social Democrats recorded modest gains at the expense of smaller parties in local elections in the state of Hesse on Sunday, a computer projection by ZDF television said.

The network said that the CDU gained 1.3 points to 33.3 percent while the SPD posted a slightly stronger gain of 1.8 percent to 38.2 percent. The smaller parties the Greens, Free Democrats (FDP) and far-right Republicans suffered losses.

The vote in Hesse, one of Germany's wealthiest states with 4.5 million eligible voters, was dominated by local issues but was expected to have national implications because it is one of only two elections in Germany this year.

Kohl, who has come under pressure because of high unemployment and the country's worsening economic troubles, has already called the Hesse poll an important foretaste for the parliamentary elections due in late 1998.
In the statewide projection, the Greens slipped 0.7 points to 10.2 percent, the FDP dropped to 4.0 percent from 5.1 percent in 1993 and the Republicans declined to 5.6 percent from 8.3 percent.

Manfred Kanther, Bonn interior minister and head of the CDU in Hesse, said results in the Hesse local election showed the CDU achieving strong gains in southern Hesse and in the cities of Frankfurt, Wiesbaden and Darmstadt.
"Overall it looks as if the CDU scored slight gains across the state," Kanther told Hessischer Rundfunk television. "If that is true that would be an exceptionally good result for the CDU.
"The SPD failed with its campaign of telling voters to settle accounts with the Bonn government. That's astonishing given the country's economic difficulties."
In the country's financial capital of Frankfurt, Kohl's CDU recorded strong gains, according to a computer projection from the Forsa polling institute.

A projection broadcast by N-TV television about one hour after polls closed at 1700 GMT showed Kohl's CDU gaining 4.2 points in Frankfurt to 37.6 percent while the SPD slipped 1.7 points to 30.3 percent.

In Frankfurt, a city of 660,000, the Greens gained 2.3 points from the last local election in 1993 to reach 16.3 percent, while the Free Democrats (FDP) were projected to receive 5.0 percent, just above their 4.4 percent in 1993.
The far-right Republicans in Frankfurt slipped to 5.9 percent from 9.3 percent.
"I'm proud that in Frankfurt the CDU was elected as a modern, big-city party," said the CDU mayor of Frankfurt, Petra Roth.
Ignatz Bubis, leader of Germany's Jewish community who led the FDP campaign in Frankfurt, said he was delighted the liberal party appeared to be headed back into city hall after a 16 year absence.

"Our first goal has been reached, we're in the Frankfurt parliament," he said. "We didn't reach our second aim which was to keep the Republicans out of the parliament and our third goal to achieve a majority for the liberals and the CDU wasn't reached either. You can't have everything."
